statements.status_notes: A flaw was found in FreeType, specifically within its CID font loader. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by tricking a user into opening content that embeds or references a specially crafted CID-keyed font. This crafted font can cause repeated allocations and decryptions of subroutine data across multiple font dictionaries, leading to excessive memory and CPU consumption. This can result in a denial of service (DoS) for the application or service processing the font, potentially causing it to hang or terminate.
statements.impact_statement: Exploitation needs the process to open an attacker-supplied CID-keyed font through the system FreeType. In the image the system libfreetype.so.6 is linked only by libfontconfig and the fc-* command-line tools. The JVM's font code (libfontmanager.so) links the FreeType copy bundled with the Temurin JDK, not the system one, and Liquibase never loads a font: it is a headless CLI whose only AWT use is GraphicsEnvironment.isHeadless() and Desktop.browse() in the report writer, neither of which initialises the font stack. Ubuntu fixed the package in 2.13.2+dfsg-1ubuntu0.2 (USN-8881-1); the next image rebuild picks it up.
